finding.claim: @inspectFile returns false (no match) whenever the external program fails to start or exits non-zero, so a request value that makes exec fail bypasses the scanner rule (fail-open).
finding.source: Attacker-controlled request value passed to the operator (e.g. REQUEST_BODY per the doc example), reaching Evaluate(tx, value) as the operator input.
finding.sink: exec.CommandContext(ctx, o.path, value).CombinedOutput() error path returning false at line 56.

trace.note: Evaluate receives attacker-influenced value
value is passed directly as an argv element to exec (no shell)
Start fails with EINVAL if value contains a NUL byte (Go syscall BytePtrFromString), or with E2BIG if value exceeds the kernel per-argument limit (~128 KiB on Linux); CombinedOutput returns err
err != nil (also ctx DeadlineExceeded for slow input) is checked
returns false, i.e. 'no match', so a deny rule does not fire

finding.guards_checked: 10s timeout (only converts to false, no fail-closed); no NUL/length validation of value; no distinction between scanner error and clean result; body limit (default 128 MiB) does not cap values below the argv limit; no fail-closed option in the operator. Case 11 (argv option injection) also applies: value is an argv element with no '--', so a value beginning with '-' is an option to the admin-configured program (secondary, program-dependent).

finding.claim: defer temp.Close() inside the per-part loop keeps one temp-file descriptor open per file part until the whole multipart body is processed, letting one request exhaust process file descriptors (DoS for concurrent transactions).
finding.source: Attacker-controlled multipart/form-data body with many parts that carry a filename= in Content-Disposition.
finding.sink: os.CreateTemp per file part, with descriptors held until ProcessRequest returns (defer at line 69).

trace.note: loop over attacker-supplied parts via mr.NextPart()
filename from Content-Disposition; non-empty means file part
os.CreateTemp opens a new fd per file part (when environment.HasAccessToFS)
defer temp.Close() is scheduled to function return, not loop iteration, so fds accumulate
on CreateTemp failure (EMFILE) the request errors out; process-wide fd exhaustion also affects other transactions

finding.guards_checked: Total body size limited by RequestBodyLimit (default 128 MiB, enforced in transaction.go before ProcessRequest); no per-request file-count limit in the processor; no explicit Close inside the loop; no ulimit handling. Impact is resource exhaustion, not code execution.

finding.claim: The per-phase transformation cache is keyed by (key-string data pointer, positional index, variable, chain id). All empty-name arguments share the same nil pointer, and their positional index is not stable (Go map iteration order in Map.FindAll and exception compaction), so a rule can receive a cached transformed value belonging to a different argument, skipping inspection of the attacker payload.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled request arguments with empty names (e.g. '=benign&=payload&k1=v&k2=v' in query or urlencoded body), plus at least one earlier rule in the same phase with the same transformation chain.
finding.sink: transformArg cache hit at rule.go:450-453 returning cached.arg as the value tested by the rule's operator.

trace.note: transformArg(arg, i, cache) with i = position in the (possibly exception-filtered) values list
argKeyPtr := unsafe.StringData(argKey); empty keys from queryUnescape/FormName have nil pointer
cache key = (nil, i, ARGS, prefixID)
cache hit returns value cached for a different empty-key argument at the same index
FindAll ranges over Go map c.data, so group order (and therefore index i) changes between calls when there are multiple key groups
exception filter (ctl:ruleRemoveTargetById) compacts matches in place, shifting indices for rules with exclusions
cache is shared by all rules in the phase (cleared per phase, not per rule)

finding.guards_checked: Cache key includes argIndex and variable, which blocks cross-variable collisions; the rulegroup.go:290-297 comment assumes a pointer uniquely identifies key content, which does not hold for empty keys; cache is per transaction phase; random ordering only matters when two or more key groups exist. Not verified by a runtime test (Bash unavailable).

finding.claim: @restpath compiles the path template without ^ or $ anchors, so a URI that merely contains the template as a substring is accepted; allowlist rules (negated @restpath) can be bypassed and ARGS_PATH can be populated from an unanchored match.
finding.sink: regexp.Compile(data) at line 50 and FindStringSubmatch(value) at line 60 used as a gate returning true on partial match.

trace.note: template '/' escaped and {placeholders} turned into (?P<name>[^?/]+), no anchors added
regexp.Compile(data) produces an unanchored pattern
FindStringSubmatch(value) matches anywhere in the URI
ARGS_PATH populated from the partial match, e.g. '/x/api/v1/users/1/delete' yields id=1

finding.guards_checked: [^?/]+ stops a placeholder from spanning a slash, but nothing constrains prefix or suffix; no anchoring in the constructor or Evaluate. Matches expexpert case 24 (validation regex without anchors). Severity depends on how deployed rules use @restpath (allowlist vs. extraction); the doc example uses it as a match gate.
